content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart Supermarkets’ Zagreb-Jarun store. I have worked in butchery since completing my vocational butcher training in 2015, including experience breaking down beef, pork and lamb, preparing meat for the counter, and serving customers.

In my current role, I bone, trim and portion carcasses, prepare fresh sausages, and advise customers on cuts and cooking times. I rotate cold-room stock using FIFO and record temperature checks twice daily. I also hold a current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate and have trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines. My earlier market-stall experience included weighing and pricing orders, operating the till, and cleaning and sanitising equipment.

FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, friendly service and food hygiene fits the way I approach my work. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my practical butchery experience, care with food-safety routines and customer service to your team.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It clearly presents the candidate’s butcher training, carcass breakdown, sausage production, customer service, FIFO rotation, temperature checks, HACCP knowledge, and apprentice-training experience. The progression from current butchery work to earlier counter-assistant duties is logical and easy to follow. It could be slightly more impactful by incorporating one or two of the strongest verified achievements, such as serving approximately 120 customers on a Saturday or producing fresh sausage at scale.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses a clean, conventional structure with standard headings and no apparent parsing obstacles. It contains important job-description terms including butcher training, beef, pork, lamb, fresh sausages, customer service, FIFO, temperature checks, HACCP, till operation, cleaning, and sanitising equipment. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the listed must-have requirements. The wording does not claim supermarket, self-service packaging, tray-sealer, or forklift experience, which is appropriate because those capabilities are not supported by the candidate information. One accuracy concern is the phrase “current HACCP” because the original information confirms renewal in 2024 but does not specify the certificate’s validity period.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong. The document shows completed butcher training and substantially exceeds the two-year meat-counter experience alternative. It also demonstrates practical HACCP-related routines through temperature logging, hygiene work, equipment sanitisation, and a HACCP basic food hygiene certificate. The letter reflects FreshCart’s stated values of knowledgeable customer service, honest advice, food hygiene, and pride in practical work. It appropriately avoids claiming experience the candidate lacks, including supermarket operations, self-service shelves, tray sealers, labelling scales, and forklift operation. The candidate does not have the nice-to-have forklift licence; this is a candidate gap rather than a document defect.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the second paragraph, replace “I also hold a current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate” with “I hold a HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate, renewed in 2024.” This precisely reflects the original candidate information without asserting an unverified current validity status.

MINOR — In the second paragraph, strengthen the evidence of customer-service impact by changing “advise customers on cuts and cooking times” to “serve approximately 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on cuts and cooking times.” This uses a verified result and better matches FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, friendly counter service.

MINOR — In the opening paragraph, consider changing “preparing meat for the counter” to “cutting, boning, trimming and portioning meat for the service counter.” This uses the job advertisement’s terminology where supported and improves keyword alignment without claiming self-service packaging experience.
critique.critical_issues: Potential unsupported wording: the cover letter states that the candidate holds a “current” HACCP certificate. The original information confirms a HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate renewed in 2024, but does not confirm its current validity period. Revise the wording as specified in the improvement instructions.

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart Supermarkets’ Zagreb-Jarun store. I have worked in butchery since completing my vocational butcher training in 2015, including experience breaking down beef, pork and lamb, cutting, boning, trimming and portioning meat for the service counter, and serving customers.

In my current role, I bone, trim and portion carcasses, prepare fresh sausages, serve approximately 120 customers on a Saturday and advise them on cuts and cooking times. I rotate cold-room stock using FIFO and record temperature checks twice daily. I hold a HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate, renewed in 2024, and have trained two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines. My earlier market-stall experience included weighing and pricing orders, operating the till, and cleaning and sanitising equipment.

FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, friendly service and food hygiene fits the way I approach my work. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my practical butchery experience, care with food-safety routines and customer service to your team.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional and well structured. It clearly presents approximately nine years of relevant butchery and meat-counter experience, practical production responsibilities, customer service, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, HACCP certification and apprentice training. The examples are specific and credible, especially the customer volume and twice-daily temperature records. It is appropriately tailored to FreshCart rather than reading as a generic letter. No material factual inconsistencies or unsupported claims were identified when compared with the original candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings and paragraphs, contains no problematic formatting, and includes relevant terms such as butcher, meat counter, beef, pork, lamb, cutting, boning, trimming, portioning, fresh sausages, customer service, FIFO, temperature checks, HACCP, till and cleaning/sanitising equipment. AI screening probability is high because the document directly connects the candidate's experience to the advertised duties and must-have requirements. It does not claim unsupported forklift, supermarket, tray-sealer or self-service-packaging experience, which is appropriate.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong. The document shows completed butcher training and substantially more than two years of meat-counter experience, HACCP knowledge, cutting and portioning, customer advice, FIFO rotation, and temperature and hygiene checks. It also reflects FreshCart's culture of knowledgeable, friendly customer service, honest product advice and pride in hygiene. The candidate's material indicates no forklift licence, so that nice-to-have remains a gap rather than a document defect. The candidate also has not worked in a supermarket or with tray sealers and self-service labelling scales; these are not listed as mandatory requirements and should not be implied.
